This movie reminded me of "Se7en" and "Law Abiding Citizen", but it's still a amazing thriller. The mystery revolving around the kidnapped daughter kept me intrigued from beginning to end, although the twist ain't very original the way it's done makes it, it's own. And one heck of a incredible twist it is. The tension between the two character is very high and it really is engrossing to watch, the script writing is also very cleverly done as well. The more stuff the plot uncovers made me more interested bit by bit until the crazy and yet great ending. Some people may gripe about the ending, but I personally really liked it. It's suspenseful thriller that is really worth watching, in fact it's one of the best suspense/thriller I seen this year with a ending that will stay with you for a long time. I don't even want to talk about the plot since the less you know the better. Sure it has few flaws, but overall I highly recommend checking this movie out.

Yongseoneun Eupda / No Mercy (2010) : Brief Review -

If that astonishing revenge thriller "Oldboy" ever had a sort of spiritual successor, then it would have looked like No Mercy. Kim Hyeong-jun's debut directorial feature, "No Mercy", actually proves the title right. Vengeance in its most brutal form! That's what it is. Park Chan-wook's astonishing "Oldboy" left me stunned, from right to left and top to bottom. I believe that Oldboy is the best revenge drama of all time, and here comes No Mercy - equally brutal and thrilling. The suspense part is a little lower than in Oldboy, and the human connect is a bit stretched away by medical terms, but the cumulative outcome is enough to leave you appalled. The film is about a serial killer who is nearly proven to be the murderer but still blackmails the forensic pathologist. To save his daughter's life, the pathologist agrees to bail him out. But is that all? No. There is a lot more behind this blackmail and there is a lot more in that unknown revenge as well. Just be prepared for the shock and brutal vengeance. Those with weak hearts should stay away from the film. Those who love and adore Korean realism in movies are more than welcome to view it. The physical and mental face-off between Sol Kyung-gu and Ryoo Seung-bum is sensible and effective. Both the actors have done well in their roles and boosted the film from their side. However, the main hero of the film is the writing. And the second hero is the director. Kim Hyeong-jun has done both the jobs here, so he is the biggest hero in this film. Way bigger than the cast and technical team. He takes the film on his shoulder like a pro, and carries the weight to its destination, despite being a newcomer to the field. Overall, No Mercy is a merciless revenge thriller that seeks more than just your attention in a 2-hour show.

RATING - 8/10*
